newsitem.title: FRANCE: Transport strikes still grip French cities.
newsitem.headline: Transport strikes still grip French cities.

text.p: Bus, tram and underground Metro train traffic was disrupted in about 10 French provincial cities on Monday as a strike over drivers' demands for early retirement and shorter hours extended into a fifth day.

The stoppages, which began with a one-day protest in about 20 major cities on Thursday, were still gripping cities including Marseille, Lille, Nice, Dijon and Le Mans. The strikes have disrupted or stopped local public transport.

Strikers are pushing for earlier retirement at the age of 55 and a reduced working week of 35 hours, with no loss of pay, reckoning that both measures would help curb record unemployment of 12.7 percent. The strike has not affected Paris.
In Toulouse, the city hardest hit, talks aimed at ending a three-week-old stoppage broke down early on Monday.
